# With spice.restack.method=merge, 'gs abort' after a conflict
# restores the changes stashed from a dirty worktree.

as 'Test <test@example.com>'
at '2024-05-27T18:24:42Z'

mkdir repo
cd repo
git init
git add init.txt dirty.txt
git commit -m 'Initial commit'
gs repo init

# use the merge method for restacks.
git config spice.restack.method merge

# create a feature branch that modifies init.
cp $WORK/extra/init.feature.txt init.txt
git add init.txt
gs bc -m feature

# go back to main and modify init in a conflicting way.
gs trunk
cp $WORK/extra/init.new.txt init.txt
git add init.txt
git commit -m 'Change init'

# make an uncommitted change to an unrelated tracked file.
gs up
cp $WORK/extra/dirty.new.txt dirty.txt
git status --porcelain
cmp stdout $WORK/golden/dirty-status.txt

# restack the feature branch: the merge conflicts.
# the dirty change was stashed out of the way.
! gs branch restack
stderr 'There was a conflict while merging'
exists .git/MERGE_HEAD
git status --porcelain
cmp stdout $WORK/golden/conflict-status.txt

# abort: the merge is gone and the uncommitted change is back.
gs abort
stderr 'Applied autostash'
! exists .git/MERGE_HEAD
git status --porcelain
cmp stdout $WORK/golden/dirty-status.txt
cmp dirty.txt $WORK/extra/dirty.new.txt
cmp init.txt $WORK/extra/init.feature.txt

# nothing was left behind in the stash list.
git stash list
! stdout .

-- repo/init.txt --
initial init

-- repo/dirty.txt --
clean dirty

-- extra/init.new.txt --
changed init

-- extra/init.feature.txt --
feature's init

-- extra/dirty.new.txt --
dirty changes

-- golden/dirty-status.txt --
 M dirty.txt
-- golden/conflict-status.txt --
UU init.txt
